sections.overview: Macaria alternata is a geometrid moth also known as the Sharp-angled Peacock; it is readily confused with its close look-alike, Macaria notata, the Peacock Moth.
sections.identification: Compared with M. notata, it usually has a deeper notch near the forewing tip and a darker, often broken edge band, but difficult specimens may need expert examination.
sections.habitat: It occurs in deciduous and mixed woodland, clearings and scrub; British records also include sand dunes.
sections.diet: Its caterpillars feed on several deciduous shrubs and trees, including willows, alder, blackthorn and sea-buckthorn.
sections.behavior: Adults are active around dusk and are attracted to lights.
sections.reproduction: In Belgium it has two adult generations from spring into late summer, and the pupa overwinters underground in a cocoon.
sections.ecology: The shared name and similar wing pattern can obscure its distinction from M. notata, so the deeper forewing notch is a useful but not infallible field clue.
sections.conservation: The sources consulted document it across several European countries but do not provide a current population trend or global threat assessment.
